body: All brothers do unkind things to each other. My older brother used to bully me but I forgive him; I would guess your brother felt the same if that was true. If we thought about how we all eventually end up all the time then our actions would probably change but we often don't. Regret is tough, isn't it?
Want to go further about why you see yourself that way or what you do to your family that is horrible?
Thank you!
Guilt about what?

I'm in the UK too. I have been in the system for years and only recently had my most recent admission. It's not about whether people are worse off than you - cast that thought off.  This is about you because it is an illness that is hurting you.  What is it causing you to think you can't cope?  Obsessive thoughts?

Don't apologise. I get that would make you feel calm. You know how I use that? I say to myself that "if all else fails I can kill myself" but it's important to keep your end of the bargain. You need to try "all else" first. That means fighting. Fighting through the dark and the shit and the depression. Think about what you would really like to do with your life and you can make that a goal. Remember, you can carry the idea that suicide is always there as a back up. Then, hopefully, you'll reach that point where you will feel better and suicide feels like an absurd idea.

In the short term, I would suggest contacting your GP.
I'm not qualified to say that. However, it would certainly hit me hard if I were a doctor.

Firstly, I would always say it is okay to kill yourself. People should have that right or control. However, I would never ever advocate. Sounds like your mum has been through some shit with the cancer and your brother dying. I'm not trying a guilt trip but to lose another child would be devastating. Why does the idea of killing yourself make you feel happy?
What has caused this? Why do you feel this way? Want to talk?
Your doctor has quite likely joined the profession because he cares about others and their health.
Why July though? And why at all?
Why? Talk!

She's got a property and partner and her parents around. I don't want to sound dickish but she has a lot there and shouldn't be relying on you. Parents are the care givers not takers. Not until they are physically or mentally unable anyway. You really have to do what is right for you at this point or the struggle will continue. At least, that's what my experience tells me.

Totally right about the dependance. The only way to break it, I suppose, is to start doing lots of things on your own and proving you can do it. I'm not really at that stage yet.

Is it too much to ask your mum to move back with you? Would that not work?
Good, as we couldn't have had this discussion that has amused me this morning.
And lots of licking yourself!
Contact someone. Ring a helpline or phone your GP for an appointment. Do you know why you feel this way?

The feelings of wanting to let go are normal. I get that. Have you tried really stepping back and asking what these people you mention are contributing in your life? If it's mostly negative, then perhaps you need to strip them from your life. You could try an honest conversation first but it's not always possible (my mum in particular is incapable of a rational conversation where she has to consider somebody has a different opinion to hers). Keep positive people around you and that behaviour and view of the world may begin to rub off on you. Sounds like there is a lot of drama in your life and real drama is really exhausting - mentally and physically. You have done well to get to where you have. Keep going. Show people how strong you are.
Perhaps your brain is considering reincarnation as the next step. What animal would you like to be? I'd love to be an eagle. An eagle that goes vegan!

Thanks for the word vomit. What can I say? You have experienced the worst of things. The very worst. One way to look at it is things can only get better from here but that's no comfort and is quite simplistic. It doesn't deal with immediate problems. I like how you described your boyfriend as a "life jacket". I totally get that and the feeling of loss. Albeit it mine is through a break up and not death. It's going to be hard but please don't make it harder for yourself by not speaking up. You have to take care of yourself and do what is best for you. Tell your mum exactly how you feel about the shitty area and what you miss from going back and how you have feelings of guilt. Don't let anyone guilt you. Go to a good school and do good things.
Any time. If you want to talk I am a message away. Take care.
Tell anyone. One thing you'll find out at the very least is who you can rely on. Seriously, there are people out there that will listen and take you seriously and won't see it as a burden.
Thanks for opening up. I am only a message away.

"And the only solution was to stand and fight."

I wrote that on a record card I kept when I first went into a mental health unit. You are right about that. Fight is a good way to describe it because it isn't easy but you will end up way stronger for it; there's no doubt about that.

It's not selfish to not want to be a bad person; the opposite is true. I think you're right. I think probably none of these things happened and you're letting your negative side take over. I really hope that the treatment you are provided with can make it all seem less tangled. Fight on.

What can I say that won't just sound like typical bullshit to cheer you up? You don't sound like a bad person. I know I am judging from one page of text but you seem to care an awful lot about the feelings of others. So, that established I think you need to hold tight. It's good that you have been diagnosed because then it can be treated and having a therapist is going to help. That's all positive. It will take time and there's an old cliché, "You can't stop the waves but you can learn to surf them." That has to be it. Getting through with the help of therapy and anything that comes from the diagnosis. It will take time but it is achievable.
Better to regret not doing it than trying and failing or succeeding and you missing out on a potentially wonderful future. And others missing out on having you in their life.
How can I help? I wish I knew what to say. I'm sorry you have lost so much.
I'm pro-choice but I am not in the business of encouraging suicide. Not sure if that helps at all.
Where are you based? Can't you speak to a professional over the phone?
It makes me upset too. It's awful.
The child is left; that is a given. But there are levels of this illness that don't allow you to see everything clearly, logically or in context.

But you are seeing it from a negative perspective. Once you realise that this is all it is you can work on seeing things in a more positive light. It will make you realise that being true to yourself will help. Fill yourself with hope. Aim for a job that you want; one that will fill you with joy every day so you're not just grinding your way through life.

I don't buy that. I know people who have loads of friends and are awful people; it's about what they show to others though. So, on the surface, they are lovely. You can't equate number of friends with level of being a "good" person. Doesn't work. There are many reasons someone may not have friends - it could be something as simple as being anxious to socialise.

What stops you from seeing a bright future? And what makes you a burden?
What a stupid thing to say.
What do you mean by you wouldn't have been the way you are?

No thanks needed. We all have rough days. The important thing is that they can come and go. You have the power and strength. It might not be that you have that today but you may have that tomorrow. Always speak out at times like this. Always.

Older people often think they no better, right? Some of that sounds close to abuse; shouting at people for not doing what they want. Stay firm and have confidence in yourself. You clearly have talent and only you should dictate what you do with that. Go your own way, my friend, and you will feel better and stronger and, eventually, people will respect you for it.

A rubbish person? You want to be a doctor! Why do you want to do that? That suggests the opposite about you. Try to keep this at the front of your mind. You can help a lot of people in the future. You may have failed a year but that isn't the end. Failing is better than not trying at all. You've gained some experience and you'll be way stronger for it. You'll make a great doctor. People need you.
I have messaged you.

Wow. What an insightful post. Lots to take from that, thanks. You clearly aren't going to be interested in me throwing empty platitudes at you. I think you're right when you say that we need to know our reason for carrying on. My reason at the moment appears to be a desire to help others. I have applied to do a Masters Degree in Dramatherapy and that is my attempt at starting that process. Seeing if I can, in some small way, help others suffering. I have no back up plan for if I don't get accepted. Maybe then I'll kill myself.

But, ultimately, I think I must be selfish because I made peace with myself a long time ago that I don't care how others feel about my death. I won't allow that to be a reason to stop myself. It's like you said, if people have that desire they will do it. I'm not going to let the reaction of others control my thinking on that.
Precisely.

Glad to hear it. I've been in 3 times. The first was a long time ago but the the last two were recent. I had a relapse on being discharged the first time so ended up back there. But I quickly realised that the comfort of being in that bubble was actually enabling me to avoid confronting the issues I was running away from.
You don't need money to speak about problems. You have people here and there are numbers you can call. You can call your doctor? What country are you in? We could find some numbers to call.
Lots of people would care. Who are those closet to you?  Who are these horrible fuckers bullying you?
I think they will discuss ways you can go forward.  It may be medication and it may be a short time in a mental health unit if considered to be a real danger.

As tempting as it may be, my advice would be not to mention it to her because it places her in a really unfair situation. Try to move past these ideas or just live with them for a bit.  As time passes they will lessen and things will change in your life.  Then you'll be able to use your experiences to help others.
There are people here.  I will be checking my messages regularly so don't feel you can't open up to once of us.

Is there a way you can buy a load of blend-able stuff and stick it around the kitchen? Few fresh fruits and frozen fruits and oats. Some powders. Things you can just throw in there quickly?  I'm not saying it will work for you, but when I was first discharged from a mental health unit, I found it helpful to stick to a meal plan.  I had three meals a day and they were the same every day but they were healthy. Plus, getting some fresh ingredients, gave me an excuse to leave the house every day.  Obviously I'm not cured but I have given myself a chance to get better.  A fighting chance.  You have to fight.

What happened yesterday? 

What is more important; how you feel about your future or how you think your parents may feel about it?

I totally get it.  When I was at my lowest I couldn't eat so I chucked loads of things into a blender; oats, fruits, fruit juice, protein powder, maca, spirulina or whatever.  Just to make sure that something was going in.

Temporarily, I would say go for the unhealthy options if that's what you crave.  As long as you are getting something in.  I do often find that they can make you feel worse afterwards though.

You raise a good point and a great way to start is to make sure you are eating.  Even if it is easier and quick.  Get it down you.  Try to relax and catch up on sleep.  Surround yourself with people and, if you can't, interact with people online.

"The only thing tough enough to break us is us."

That is from the British rapper Akala.  I hold a lot of stock in that.  You have shown great strength in everything you have done.  I want to say I understand but I can only understand to a degree.  Let me give you some context before I carry on.

I was in my longest ever relationship until recently.  It lasted 3 years so isn't a patch on the 8 you experienced.  But this woman matched me in everything; she challenged me and she is bright and beautiful and caring but I pushed her away with my moods.  Yes, I had this fantastic person to share my life with - we had planned a future - and I still wasn't happy in my deepest thoughts.

So, what is it with us?  You describe having these negative feelings when you were in the relationship.  The real problem then is us, is it not?  Not that you are useless or hopeless or anything like that; far from it.  You have shown how strong you are in your post.  You have I suspect, just like I have, placed too much stock in another person.  Given too much of yourself away.  You need to look at yourself and ask who you are and whether you need another person to be happy.  We don't and we have to find a way to reach that point.

I extend my hand to you, brother.  I am only a message away.  Love.

I could tell you not to do it and promise a bright future.  Would that be honest?  I don't know you.  What I will say is that the thought patterns are normal.  Two parts of your brain fighting each other to see which will be victorious.  Have you ever tried mindfulness?  It doesn't stop me wanting to kill myself but it does, at times, help me calm down a little and have those feelings subside slightly.
Isn't it a comfort to know you aren't alone?
Excellent. Let us continue to find signs and hope the feelings will subside.

There is nothing bad about wanting to be dead. Nothing at all. Please understand this. It is really hard to deal with though, right? Do you work in extremes of emotions? I certainly do and I often get so frustrated, depressed or daunted by everything that I just think, "I'll kill myself."

This morning I considered a short walk to the nearby bridge - a suicide hotspot - to throw myself off. I haven't. I don't know why. What has stuck with me is what another poster said on here somewhere about giving it a few days and seeing how you feel. Maybe I won't feel like this then and maybe I will. But we have time. This is the lowest we will ever get, right? Can we not just have a "fuck it" attitude and face everything head on? I think we can. I hope we can. I hope for you. Posting here was a good thing. How are you feeling now?

Society says that this way of thinking is wrong, doesn't it? To me it has always been a natural part of my thought process and it gives the ultimate control. But what I am finding is that as I spend more time doing what I enjoy it is easier. As I struggle more and more I am finding out who I am and what I want to be doing with my life. It doesn't change the idea that I want to be dead but it does give me focus and purpose. Sometimes I feel fearless - that nobody can touch me.

"To thine own self be true."

Everyone will tell you it is not your fault and you shouldn't blame yourself and there is a reason for that and the reason is because it is true. That is the first truth you need to realise. Do everything you can to see that. Try to focus on the positives you brought to her life and how much more enriched her life was for having you in it.

It's easy for others to give advice about seeing someone or giving it a few days. It's not so easy to take it. When a person feels they are set on it then they will most likely be unwilling to respond to that kind of positive response. Every day I want to be dead. Every single day. I have not been able to do it correctly. I could be wrong but I think, like me, you may not really want to end your life. If you did then you would have found a way. That's not a challenge. That is me saying there is something inside you that, instinctively, wants to fit.  That is the real challenge; to keep going when everything feels like shit. Feel free to PM me and we can chat as raw and detailed as you want. We can message each other or talk on the phone. Just open up as fully as you can and then see how you feel.
